finding.title: Paused HTTP/1 stream producers can leave response bytes buffered
finding.impact: The HTTP/1 chunked writer could wait indefinitely for another producer frame while response headers or a completed chunk remained buffered below it. A long-lived SSE or streamed response could therefore stall a client and retain connection or application state until another chunk or stream completion arrived. No confidentiality, integrity, authentication, or authorization bypass was demonstrated.
prerequisites: The response uses the native HTTP/1 chunked writer, normally through TLS.
The producer pauses after opening the response or after emitting a chunk.
The underlying asynchronous writer retains bytes until an explicit flush or later write.

initial_fail_first.result: A real TLS response chunk was not readable within 250 ms while its producer remained open.

expanded_fail_first.result: Both headers before the first chunk and a complete SSE chunk before producer completion timed out over a bounded real TLS channel.

initial_per_chunk_confirmation.result: Explicit header and per-chunk flushes established timely delivery and fail-closed stream behavior, but this was not retained as the final implementation because it unnecessarily flushed every ready chunk.

coalescing_fail_first.result: Three prequeued chunks caused five flushes instead of the expected two: one header flush and one completed body batch.

coverage: HTTP/1 TLS headers are readable before the first response chunk exists.
A complete SSE chunk is readable while the producer remains open.
Header, midstream, and terminal flush failures propagate and close the response stream.
Immediately queued chunks coalesce without changing exact chunked wire bytes.
Continuously ready output is bounded to 64 chunks or 16 KiB before a flush.

sandbox_only_observation.reason: The restricted sandbox denied loopback socket operations with PermissionDenied. The identical command passes outside that sandbox.

protocol_contract.response_headers: Headers are flushed once before waiting for the first producer frame.
protocol_contract.paused_producer: If no response frame is immediately ready after writing a chunk, queued bytes are flushed before awaiting the producer.
protocol_contract.ready_producer: Immediately available frames are coalesced while preserving order and exact HTTP/1 chunk framing.
protocol_contract.completion: The terminal zero chunk is written and flushed as before.
protocol_contract.errors: Every write or flush error closes the response reader and is returned to the connection loop.
unchanged: response body bytes and chunk order

methodology.investigation_rule: Investigate when candidate median delta is below -5%, or candidate and baseline ranges do not overlap while candidate is slower.
methodology.correctness_rule: Require exact samples and byte counts, zero sample errors, expected reused connection counts, and no protocol, internal, body-timeout, or idle-timeout counter deltas.
methodology.gbit_definition: Total application request and response bytes divided by lifecycle elapsed; this is not wire bandwidth.
methodology.unchanged_inputs: Both variants use identical AOT router/client executables, TLS, payloads, driver, timeouts, retry policy, worker counts, runtime thread counts, and performance thresholds. Only the frozen native library changes.
methodology.host: Shared Darwin arm64 host. Unrelated VM and emulator activity is recorded in each retained run; no audit-owned build, test, or inference task overlapped timing.

first_campaign_preflight_stop.status: No warmup or timed variant started; retained and not rerun in place.
first_campaign_preflight_stop.disposition: The unchanged quiet-host threshold rejected the run. No external process or threshold was changed.

h1_stream_one_chunk.shape: 2000 serial requests; 1 KiB request and response; one response chunk

h1_stream_large_chunks.shape: 256 requests at concurrency 4; 256 KiB request; 1 MiB response in eight 128 KiB chunks

h1_stream_small_chunks.shape: 256 requests at concurrency 4; 4 KiB request; 64 KiB response in 256-byte chunks

complete_comparison.interpretation: No material throughput, tail-latency, memory, connection-accounting, or selected transport-counter regression is reproduced. The small-chunk improvement is consistent with draining immediately queued frames without an awaited receive for every chunk, but the campaign does not prove a sole causal mechanism.

performance.clearance: SA-011 affected-path performance is locally cleared for the measured TLS HTTP/1 one-chunk, eight-chunk, and 256-chunk response shapes. This is not proof of identical timing, wire throughput, audit-wide performance clearance, or resolution of earlier negative comparisons.

full_verify.note: Fresh verification passed without changing a test timeout, retry policy, response batching bound, performance threshold, TLS setting, or protocol rule.

local_companions.detail: Focused local-model test advice could not reach Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434 or GLM at 127.0.0.1:18080 because both loopback connections were denied with EPERM. No sandbox bypass was attempted.

remaining: The fix does not add HTTP/1 request chunked decoding or clear deployment-specific proxy differential behavior.
Direct timing of final SA-010 candidate 1a6d317f remains separate pending evidence.
Earlier security-audit performance findings, finite handle availability, and unreviewed component rows remain open.
A local benchmark cannot prove identical performance across production hosts or workloads.
